title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 8
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Annual appointments and consulting rooms at five clinics:

Ashgrove: 8,400 appointments, 12 rooms
Bramfield: 14,200 appointments, 26 rooms
Cheddon: 5,100 appointments, 6 rooms
Dunkeld: 11,700 appointments, 20 rooms
Ewhurst: 9,600 appointments, 15 rooms

Which clinic handles the most appointments per consulting room?
options: A. Ashgrove
B. Bramfield
C. Cheddon
D. Dunkeld
E. Ewhurst
questions.explanation: Appointments divided by rooms: Ashgrove 700, Bramfield 546, Cheddon 850, Dunkeld 585, Ewhurst 640. Cheddon is highest. The clinic with the most appointments also has the most rooms, so it is not the most heavily worked per room.

questions.prompt:
Annual membership of a society:

2021: 4,820
2022: 4,410
2023: 4,390
2024: 3,690
2025: 3,520

In which year was the percentage fall from the previous year the largest?
options: D. Membership rose in one of the years
questions.explanation: Year on year: 2022 -8.5%, 2023 -0.5%, 2024 -15.9%, 2025 -4.6%. 2024 is the largest fall at -15.9%. 2022 loses a similar number of members but from a larger base.

questions.prompt:
A college's income by source:

Tuition: 44%
Accommodation: 23%
Research: 14%
Grants: 10%
Trading: 6%
Other: 3%

What is the smallest number of sources that together account for at least 85% of income?
options: A. Four
B. Two
C. Three
D. Five
E. Six
questions.explanation: Largest first: 44 + 23 + 14 = 81%, short of 85. Adding Grants reaches 91%. So 4 sources are needed.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 22, 26, 26, 29, 31, 35, 74

Which statement about these readings is accurate?
options: A. The mode is greater than the median
B. The mean is smaller than the median
C. The mean and the median are equal
D. The range is greater than the mean
E. The mode and the mean are equal
questions.explanation: Mean is 243/7 = 34.71; median is the fourth value, 29; mode is 26; range is 52. The range exceeds the mean, and the mean exceeds the median because of the single large reading.

questions.prompt:
Two insurance policies:

Policy A: premium GBP 180.00, excess GBP 500.00 on any claim
Policy B: premium GBP 260.00, excess GBP 150.00 on any claim

Select the cheaper policy for a year with no claim AND the cheaper policy for a year with exactly one claim.
options: A. Policy A with no claim; Policy A with one claim
B. Policy A with no claim; Policy B with one claim
C. Policy B with no claim; Policy A with one claim
D. Policy B with no claim; Policy B with one claim
E. The two cost the same in both cases
questions.explanation: With no claim only the premium is paid: GBP 180.00 against GBP 260.00, so Policy A is cheaper. With one claim the excess is added: GBP 680.00 against GBP 410.00, so Policy B is cheaper. The lower premium carries the higher excess.

questions.prompt:
Cleaning can be done by employed staff at GBP 31,200.00 a year in wages plus GBP 4,800.00 for equipment, or by a contractor at GBP 2,950.00 a month.

Select the cheaper option over one year AND the annual difference.
options: A. Employing cleaners; GBP 600.00
B. Employing cleaners; GBP 2,000.00
C. Using the contractor; GBP 1,200.00
D. Using the contractor; GBP 600.00
E. The two cost the same over a year
questions.explanation: Employed staff cost GBP 31,200.00 + GBP 4,800.00 = GBP 36,000.00. The contractor costs 12 × GBP 2,950.00 = GBP 35,400.00. Using the contractor is cheaper by GBP 600.00 a year.

questions.prompt:
Two market stalls yesterday:

Stall A: 420 items sold, average price GBP 7.40
Stall B: 145 items sold, average price GBP 19.60

Select the stall with the higher takings AND the stall with the higher average price.
options: A. Stall A on takings; Stall B on average price
B. Stall A on both measures
C. Stall B on takings; Stall A on average price
D. Stall B on both measures
E. The two stalls are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Takings: Stall A GBP 3,108.00, Stall B GBP 2,842.00. Average price is given: Stall A GBP 7.40, Stall B GBP 19.60. Volume and price point to different stalls, so neither figure alone ranks them.

questions.prompt:
A tour operator has fixed costs of GBP 32,400.00 a season. Each place sells for GBP 148.00 and costs GBP 76.00 to provide.

Select the number of places needed to break even AND the number needed for a profit of GBP 18,000.00.
options: A. 450 to break even; 900 for the target
B. 400 to break even; 700 for the target
C. 450 to break even; 800 for the target
D. 300 to break even; 600 for the target
E. 450 to break even; 700 for the target
questions.explanation: Contribution is GBP 72.00 a place. Break-even is GBP 32,400.00 / GBP 72.00 = 450 places. Covering GBP 50,400.00 needs 700 places.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): pupils on roll — School A 940, School B 1,480, School C 620

SOURCE 2 (table): pupils taking a school meal — School A 612, School B 802, School C 447

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The catering review should start with the school where take-up is the highest share of the roll."

Which school should the review start with?
options: A. School A
B. School B
C. School C
D. The three schools are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Take-up rates: School A 65.1%, School B 54.2%, School C 72.1%. School C is highest. School B serves the most meals in total and has by far the largest roll.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "The waiting list has fallen from 4,200 to 2,600 since the new booking system."

SOURCE 2 (note): "Under the new system, patients who have not confirmed within 14 days are removed from the list and must re-refer."

SOURCE 3 (table): re-referrals rose from 180 to 1,510 over the same period.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Much of the fall reflects patients being removed and re-referred rather than treated
B. Waiting times have halved
C. The new system treated 1,600 additional patients
D. The waiting list is now counted weekly
E. Re-referrals are unrelated to the change
questions.explanation: The list fell by 1,600 while re-referrals rose by 1,330, and Source 2 supplies the mechanism connecting them. Option C assumes the fall equals treatment, which is exactly what the other two sources undercut.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): units produced — Line 1 22,400, Line 2 6,100, Line 3 13,800

SOURCE 2 (table): rejection rate — Line 1 0.9%, Line 2 4.8%, Line 3 2.2%

SOURCE 3 (email): "Each rejected unit costs the same to scrap, so start where the most units are rejected."

Which line should be tackled first?
options: A. Line 1
B. Line 3
C. Line 2
D. All three reject the same number
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Rejected units are output multiplied by rate: Line 1 202, Line 2 293, Line 3 304. Line 3 is highest. Line 2 has much the worst rate but the smallest output.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Wages at the firm rose 14% over five years."

SOURCE 2 (table): the price index rose from 100 to 119 over the same five years.

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board asks whether staff are better off."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Staff are 14% better off
B. Staff are about 33% better off
C. The comparison cannot be made from these sources
D. Staff are slightly worse off in real terms
E. Prices and wages rose by the same amount
questions.explanation: Real wages are 1.14 / 1.19 = 95.8% of their starting level, a fall of about 4%. Source 1 alone supports option A, which is why the price index is the decisive source.

questions.prompt:
A shop sold 80 shirts, some at GBP 25.00 and the rest at GBP 40.00. How many were sold at GBP 40.00?

(1) Takings were GBP 2,600.00.
(2) Equal numbers were sold at each price.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1): 25(80 - x) + 40x = 2,600 gives 2,000 + 15x = 2,600, so x = 40 - sufficient. From (2): equal numbers means 40 at each price - also sufficient. Both statements describe the same sale, and either alone answers the question.

questions.prompt:
How many hours was a shop open last week?

(1) It opened for the same number of hours on each of six days.
(2) It opened for a total of 54 hours.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) fixes the pattern but not the amount: six equal days could be any length. (2) states the total directly, which is what the question asks.

questions.prompt:
What is the price of one chair?

(1) Four chairs and one table cost GBP 520.00.
(2) Two chairs and one table cost GBP 340.00.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Neither statement alone has enough equations for two unknowns. Subtracting gives two chairs = GBP 180.00, so a chair is GBP 90.00 and a table GBP 160.00 - consistent with both.

questions.prompt:
Is the integer x greater than 5?

(1) x squared is greater than 25.
(2) x is negative.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) allows x above 5 or below −5. (2) alone says nothing about magnitude. Together, x is negative and beyond −5, so it is certainly not greater than 5 — a definite "no", which is sufficiency.

questions.prompt:
Which depot earns the most revenue per van?

Depot | Vans | Late deliveries per 100 | Annual revenue | Customer rating
Ardley | 86 | 4.2 | GBP 268,000.00 | 74
Bunwell | 143 | 2.7 | GBP 421,000.00 | 66
Crowhurst | 61 | 6.1 | GBP 196,000.00 | 80
Dowsby | 118 | 3.4 | GBP 352,000.00 | 71
Edgcott | 172 | 1.9 | GBP 498,000.00 | 59
Fritwell | 97 | 5 | GBP 291,000.00 | 83
options: A. Crowhurst
B. Ardley
C. Bunwell
D. Dowsby
E. Edgcott
questions.explanation: Revenue divided by vans: Ardley GBP 3,116.28, Bunwell GBP 2,944.06, Crowhurst GBP 3,213.11, Dowsby GBP 2,983.05, Edgcott GBP 2,895.35, Fritwell GBP 3,000.00. Crowhurst is highest. The depot with the largest revenue also runs the most vans.

questions.prompt:
How many depots have a late-delivery rate above the mean for the six?

Depot | Vans | Late deliveries per 100 | Annual revenue | Customer rating
Ardley | 86 | 4.2 | GBP 268,000.00 | 74
Bunwell | 143 | 2.7 | GBP 421,000.00 | 66
Crowhurst | 61 | 6.1 | GBP 196,000.00 | 80
Dowsby | 118 | 3.4 | GBP 352,000.00 | 71
Edgcott | 172 | 1.9 | GBP 498,000.00 | 59
Fritwell | 97 | 5 | GBP 291,000.00 | 83
options: A. Two
B. Three
C. One
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: Mean late-delivery rate is (4.2 + 2.7 + 6.1 + 3.4 + 1.9 + 5) / 6 = 3.88. Above it: Ardley 4.2, Crowhurst 6.1, Fritwell 5 — 3 depots.

questions.prompt:
Taking the rate as late deliveries per 100 vans a week, which depot records the most late deliveries a week?

Depot | Vans | Late deliveries per 100 | Annual revenue | Customer rating
Ardley | 86 | 4.2 | GBP 268,000.00 | 74
Bunwell | 143 | 2.7 | GBP 421,000.00 | 66
Crowhurst | 61 | 6.1 | GBP 196,000.00 | 80
Dowsby | 118 | 3.4 | GBP 352,000.00 | 71
Edgcott | 172 | 1.9 | GBP 498,000.00 | 59
Fritwell | 97 | 5 | GBP 291,000.00 | 83
options: A. Ardley
B. Bunwell
C. Dowsby
D. Fritwell
E. Edgcott
questions.explanation: Late deliveries are vans multiplied by the rate per hundred vans: Ardley 361, Bunwell 386, Crowhurst 372, Dowsby 401, Edgcott 327, Fritwell 485. Fritwell is highest. The worst rate belongs to Crowhurst, which runs the fewest vans.

questions.prompt:
Rank the depots by revenue and separately by customer rating, highest first in each. Which depot's two ranks differ most?

Depot | Vans | Late deliveries per 100 | Annual revenue | Customer rating
Ardley | 86 | 4.2 | GBP 268,000.00 | 74
Bunwell | 143 | 2.7 | GBP 421,000.00 | 66
Crowhurst | 61 | 6.1 | GBP 196,000.00 | 80
Dowsby | 118 | 3.4 | GBP 352,000.00 | 71
Edgcott | 172 | 1.9 | GBP 498,000.00 | 59
Fritwell | 97 | 5 | GBP 291,000.00 | 83
options: A. Ardley
B. Bunwell
C. Crowhurst
D. Fritwell
E. Edgcott
questions.explanation: By revenue: Edgcott, Bunwell, Dowsby, Fritwell, Ardley, Crowhurst. By rating: Fritwell, Crowhurst, Ardley, Dowsby, Bunwell, Edgcott. Rank gaps: Ardley 2, Bunwell 3, Crowhurst 4, Dowsby 1, Edgcott 5, Fritwell 3. Edgcott differs by 5.
